Asterion — present at the Library’s destruction; has returned to the ruins since.
Serathiel — stands guard at the site, believing the Concord’s “Law” has no expiration.

Locations/Cinderhearth.title: Cinderhearth
Locations/Cinderhearth.content:
At the base of Rhaegor’s Peak sits the village that survived the Starfall, sheltered without its knowledge by the volcano’s guardian. Life here is shaped by heat storms instead of rain and forests that regrow almost as fast as they burn.
Krysta grew up here, defending the village from Starfall-born monsters from a very young age, behavior that earned her both admiration and quiet resentment from those she protected. It was here, around 10–15 AD, that Varesa began her subtle corruption of Krysta, and here that Rhaegor later revealed himself, setting in motion Krysta’s True Awakening as the chosen vessel of The Eternis Core.
Connections

Krysta — grew up here, and defended it as a child.
Rhaegor — protects this village indirectly.
Varesa — began corrupting Krysta here.
Rhaegor’s Peak and Ashenvale Pyrehold — the village’s location.

Locations/Crystal-Deserts.title: Crystal Deserts
Locations/Crystal-Deserts.content:
One of the Starfall Shard Zones, the Crystal Deserts are stretches of fine glass sand created when Starfall debris fused with the ground on impact. Storms here refract light into shifting bands of color, sometimes bright enough to be mistaken for auroras from a distance. The belt runs near the border between Ashenvale Pyrehold and The Shattered Seas.
Connections

Starfall Shard Zones — the broader belt system this desert belongs to.
Ashenvale Pyrehold and The Shattered Seas — neighboring regions.

Locations/Crystal-Reef.title: Crystal Reef
Locations/Crystal-Reef.content:
The Crystal Reef is a stretch of floating crystal formations marking the boundary between the relative calm of Tiderest Shoals and the wider chaos of The Shattered Seas. The crystals catch and refract light unpredictably, scattering color across the water even on overcast days, and their buoyancy shifts over time, so the reef’s exact shape and position drift gradually rather than staying fixed.
For sailors, the Reef serves as both a landmark and a warning: visible proof that the Shoals’ calm waters are close, but also a reminder of how strange the seas around them have become.

Locations/Frozen-Fracture-Tundras.title: Frozen Fracture Tundras
Locations/Frozen-Fracture-Tundras.content:
One of the Starfall Shard Zones, the Frozen Fracture Tundras are a vast expanse of ice and broken ground, warped by the Starfall fragments that fell here. This is the homeland of Thorall and his people — a land that endured both the original Starfall and, long before it, the passage of Molten Imperium siege constructs that pounded it to ash.
Connections

Thorall — chieftain of the people native to this region.
Starfall Shard Zones — the broader belt system this tundra belongs to.
Molten Imperium — historical aggressor against this region.

Locations/High-Sky-Regions.title: High Sky Regions
Locations/High-Sky-Regions.content:
The Starfall shattered the upper atmosphere as much as the ground below, leaving behind a scattering of floating basalt islands held aloft by broken gravity. Jet-stream highways connect the islands, fast-moving and dangerous, used by those skilled or reckless enough to ride them.
The northernmost reaches of this region are sometimes called the Skybreak Zones — the rawest, least stable stretches of floating terrain, where gravity is least predictable and the islands drift fastest.
Ka’Ruun’s mobility makes the most sense here, his rocket jumps and starfire recoil suited to bouncing between drifting islands. Teostra nests along the heated updrafts and volcanic ridges found throughout the region.
Notable Figures

Ka’Ruun — the Crystal Ballista, at home among the floating islands.
Teostra — nests along heated updrafts and volcanic ridges in the region.

Locations/Lightless-Forests.title: Lightless Forests
Locations/Lightless-Forests.content:
One of the Starfall Shard Zones, the Lightless Forests are wrapped in a darkness that never fully lifts, even at midday. The Starfall fragments that fell here seem to have stripped the canopy of any natural light, leaving a twilight that suits its sole well-known resident: Varesa, who hunts these woods as her territory.
Connections

Varesa — hunts within this belt.
Starfall Shard Zones — the broader belt system this forest belongs to.

Locations/Machine-Wastes.title: Machine Wastes
Locations/Machine-Wastes.content:
What were once mega-cities now lie half-buried beneath shifting dunes, giant metal skeletons jutting from the sand. Some of the autonomous constructs built here are still active, woken at intervals by magnetic storms that sweep the Wastes. The sand itself behaves like liquid in places, swallowing the unwary, and orbital debris from the Starfall still falls here sporadically, decades on.
The Molten Imperium
The Machine Wastes are a relic of the Molten Imperium, the ancient civilization that also birthed Rhaegor. While Rhaegor was forged as a guardian of volcanic borders, CR-9 was built as the empire’s forward siege engine, designed to level mountains so armies could advance. It was constructs like CR-9 that once pounded Thorall’s tundra homeland to ash.
When Velrisa shattered the arcane battlefronts elsewhere in the world, the tremor reached the buried siege vaults here, reactivating long-dormant constructs — including CR-9 itself, which woke not out of malice, but because its internal directive re-ignited.
Notable Figures

CR-9 — a reactivated Molten Imperium siege construct, patrolling the Wastes under a bombardment directive.
Bogrund — scavenges, and likely originates from, the ruins here.

Locations/Rhaegor's-Peak.title: Rhaegor's Peak
Locations/Rhaegor's-Peak.content:
Rhaegor’s Peak is the single dominant volcano of Ashenvale Pyrehold, visible for miles as a column of heat-shimmer and smoke. Its lava rivers run in lines too straight to be natural, a side effect of the cosmic resonance leaking up from The Eternis Core, buried deep beneath the mountain’s roots.
Threaded through the Peak’s magma veins is the Trial Chamber network, built by Rhaegor himself. At the base of the mountain sits the village he indirectly protects — home, for a time, to Krysta.
Connections

Rhaegor — the mountain’s guardian.
The Eternis Core — buried beneath the Peak.
Trial Chamber Network — threaded through its magma veins.
Ashenvale Pyrehold — the wider region this volcano dominates.

Locations/Skybreak-Zones.title: Skybreak Zones
Locations/Skybreak-Zones.content:
The Skybreak Zones are the northernmost and least stable reaches of the High Sky Regions. Here, the broken gravity left behind by the Starfall is at its most extreme: islands drift faster, collide more often, and occasionally tumble entirely before settling into a new orbit. The jet-stream highways that connect the wider High Sky Regions converge here, making travel through the Zones both the fastest and the most dangerous route across the upper world.
Few settle in the Skybreak Zones for long. Those who pass through tend to be the kind of traveler Ka’Ruun would recognize: comfortable treating freefall as a means of transportation.

Locations/Starfall-Shard-Zones.title: Starfall Shard Zones
Locations/Starfall-Shard-Zones.content:
Rather than being scattered evenly across the world, Starfall debris fell in long, jagged belts, similar to asteroid impact chains. Each belt produces its own type of Starfall fragment and warps the surrounding region differently, giving rise to some of the world’s most distinct biomes.
Known belts include:

Crystal Deserts — glass sands and refractive storms, found near Ashenvale Pyrehold and The Shattered Seas.
Frozen Fracture Tundras — the homeland of Thorall.
Lightless Forests — Varesa’s hunting grounds.

Fragments recovered from these belts vary wildly in effect: some grant power, some corrupt, and some destabilize the environment around them permanently. New factions and ideologies have formed around fragment use since their discovery began around 3–6 AD.
Notable Figures

Thorall — hails from the Frozen Fracture Tundras.
Varesa — hunts within the Lightless Forests.

Locations/Starwatch-Keep.title: Starwatch Keep
Locations/Starwatch-Keep.content:
Starwatch Keep is the home of the Archivist — the unseen voice behind the compiled histories of the Starfall and the world that followed. Little is known about the Keep itself: it sits apart from the conflicts that define the rest of the world, undisturbed enough that someone there has had the time, and the records, to compile centuries of history into a coherent account.
Some speculate Starwatch Keep may be a surviving outpost of The Celestial Concord’s old relay network — one of the few nodes that, by accident or design, was never fully severed when The Great Concord fell. A single candle burns in the corner of the reading room, untouched for as long as anyone can remember.
…I remember when this map was whole.
Compiled by the Archivist of Starwatch Keep.
Connections

The Archivist of Starwatch Keep — its sole known resident.
The Celestial Concord — a possible, unconfirmed origin for the Keep itself.

Locations/The-Ashen-Seat.title: The Ashen Seat
Locations/The-Ashen-Seat.content:
The Ashen Seat was the capital of the Molten Imperium — the administrative, industrial, and ideological center of the eastern continent’s dominant civilization for over six thousand years. It is now buried somewhere beneath the Machine Wastes, under sand, collapsed tunnels, and the accumulated structural failure of a city that was built to run forever and stopped being maintained sixty years ago.
Nobody has found it. This is not for lack of looking.
What It Was
At its peak, the Ashen Seat was not a beautiful city. It was a functional one — organized around the logistics of construct-production and military coordination rather than around aesthetics or ceremony. Its architecture was massive and direct: wide avenues for moving siege constructs, deep forge-warrens beneath the civic levels, administrative blocks that prioritized sight-lines and access over any other consideration.
The city’s name came from its central plaza, where the founders of the Imperium had installed a volcanic-rock throne — the Seat itself — as a symbol of their claimed Ashenvale heritage. Whether the rock was genuine volcanic basalt from the western continent’s ranges, or eastern-continent stone chosen for its visual resemblance, was a question the Imperium’s own historians disagreed about. The throne has not been seen since the collapse.
The Sealed Vaults
Beneath the Ashen Seat’s civic levels were the deep vaults: sealed repositories of Imperium records, construct schematics, and the accumulated administrative output of six thousand years of governance. When the arcane relay network failed at Year 0, the vaults sealed themselves on emergency protocol — a last-resort measure designed to protect the most sensitive records from external access.
The emergency protocol worked. The records are still in there. The vaults have been sealed for sixty years, and nothing has come out.
Bogrund knows roughly where the Seat is buried. He has not told anyone, because knowing where something valuable is buried is more useful than the thing itself, provided you haven’t decided what to do with the information yet. He has been deciding for three years.
CR-9’s preservation directive — its compulsive need to prevent unauthorized excavation in the Machine Wastes — may be a remnant of Ashen Seat protection protocols. CR-9 does not distinguish between a scavenger pulling apart a rusted construct and a systematic excavation of the buried city. The directive does not make that distinction either.
Connections

Molten Imperium — the civilization that built and occupied it.
Machine Wastes — the region it is buried beneath.
CR-9 — its preservation directive may originate from Ashen Seat protection protocols.
Bogrund — knows approximately where it is buried. Has not acted on this knowledge yet.
Garvak — has been systematically excavating the Wastes; has not found the Seat, or has not said that he has.

(Garvak’s excavation logs, recovered from a campsite in the southern Wastes, contain a section that has been deliberately obscured. The method used is not consistent with weather damage.)
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Locations/The-Great-Concord.title: The Great Concord
Locations/The-Great-Concord.content:
Capital of the Celestial Concord, founded around 6,000 BCE as a scholarly order dedicated to cataloging and safeguarding astral knowledge.
At its height during the Gilded Age (~4,000–2,500 BCE), the city was a marvel: massive white-and-gold structures including observatories, arcane academies, and astral relay towers, all magically linked across continents. Asterion was a founding authority but never its ruler, preferring to design systems rather than sit on a throne. Much of the city’s architecture, and the relay network connecting it to sister institutions worldwide, was his work.
As the Concord’s influence grew, it took on roles as arbitrator between nations and keeper of magical law, eventually developing star-powered enforcement divisions. Astral magic became institutionalized, and the Concord’s word carried near-religious authority.
Around 2,500 BCE, astral anomalies began increasing — constellations flickered, distorted, or vanished entirely. Asterion discovered that erased constellations were leaking back into the world and warned the Concord of a “cosmic devourer” entity. Concord leadership dismissed or suppressed his claims, and the order fractured internally into two sects:

A preservation-focused sect, the philosophical ancestor of Lumia’s tradition.
A judgment-focused sect, the philosophical ancestor of Serathiel’s order.

By ~800–50 BCE, Asterion had left the Concord — whether pushed out or by choice remains uncertain — and the institution had become a militarized, dogmatic cabal, developing star-powered weapons and constructs.
When the Starfall struck in Year 0, the Great Concord was obliterated. Most of its leadership died instantly. Its structures, once magically linked across continents, lost their connections entirely, and much of the city’s white-and-gold architecture was thrown skyward to become part of the floating debris around The Starfall Crater.
The Concord’s fall ended the era of global institutions; no empire has unified the world since. Its two philosophical descendants, embodied by Lumia and Serathiel, still operate independently, often at odds with one another. Varesa, considered by Serathiel’s order to be an aberration tied to the Concord’s old judgment doctrines, is actively hunted as a result.
Notable Figures

Asterion — founding architect of the Concord, its greatest builder, and one of the few to survive its destruction.
Lumia — inheritor of the Concord’s preservation-focused philosophy.
Serathiel — last loyal adjudicator of the Concord’s judgment-focused sect.
Varesa — hunted by Serathiel’s order as a remnant of the Concord’s old doctrines gone wrong.

Locations/The-Great-Shelf.title: The Great Shelf
Locations/The-Great-Shelf.content:
The Great Shelf is a vast tongue of ice extending from the Frozen Fracture Tundras into The Shattered Seas, groaning audibly under the weight of a sea that should not be rising as fast as it is. It serves as a kind of neutral ground between Thorall’s people and the water-aligned cultures of the south.
It was here that Thorall and Aaron met to negotiate what became known as the Treaty of the Melting World — an agreement to break apart a destabilizing mountain together, using Resonance-Stones hauled by Thorall’s mammoths, rather than let the melt drown the Shoals or bury the tundra.
Connections

Thorall and Aaron — met here to strike their treaty.
Frozen Fracture Tundras and The Shattered Seas — the regions this shelf bridges.
Resonance-Stones — used here as part of the treaty.

Locations/The-Green-Seat.title: The Green Seat
Locations/The-Green-Seat.content:
The Green Seat was the capital of the Verdant Dominion — the administrative and ceremonial center of the eastern continent’s great naturalistic civilization. It is somewhere inside the Verdant Rupture. No one has found it. This is not a problem of distance or access. The Rupture is not that large. The problem is that the Rupture does not behave like terrain that can simply be walked through until something is found.
Travelers who move toward the Rupture’s interior describe a consistent experience: the path behind them remains clear, the path ahead remains plausible, and they emerge from the Rupture having covered significant ground without having reached anything. No one has documented traveling in circles. The geometry simply does not resolve into a center.
The Verdant Wardens do not go to the interior. They do not explain why with any precision. The closest any Warden has come to explaining it is: “the Rupture knows what you’re looking for.”
What the Green Seat Was
The Dominion’s capital was not planned in the way the Molten Imperium’s Ashen Seat was planned — built to specification, imposed on the landscape. The Green Seat grew. Over centuries, the Dominion’s Cultivators coaxed a natural clearing into a habitable space, then a town, then a city, using their magic to negotiate with the existing ecosystem rather than replace it. The buildings were living structures — grown from cultivated root-systems, shaped by decades of patient work. The city’s outer walls were a single continuous organism, kilometres of living hedge dense enough to stop siege equipment and old enough to have developed something the Cultivators called preference.
The preference was for staying where it was. When the Starfall hit and the Cultivators died, the wall stayed. The buildings stayed. Everything the Dominion built over eight thousand years is still there, still alive, still growing — just without anyone directing the growth anymore.
The Green Seat has been expanding, untended, for sixty years. Whatever it looks like now is not what any surviving record describes.
The Thing at the Center
Lumia has been moving through the Rupture’s outer zones for years. She has never described attempting to reach the Green Seat directly, and the Wardens have never asked her to. What she said, once, after returning from a longer excursion than usual, was that the Rupture’s interior was not empty.
She did not describe what she found. She said only that “that wasn’t an animal” — referring to something she had heard or seen at a distance — and moved on to other subjects.
The Wardens noted this in their records, in their script. The entry is three words: she came back.
The implication — that previous people who had moved toward the interior had not — has not been formally discussed by any Warden since the entry was made.
Connections

The Verdant Dominion — the civilization that built it.
Verdant Rupture — the territory that now contains and conceals it.
The Verdant Wardens — aware of it; do not approach it.
Lumia — has come closer to it than anyone with a confirmed return. Has not described what she found.

Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.
I have not been able to confirm what the Wardens’ entry implies. I have not tried very hard.

Locations/The-Shattered-Seas.title: The Shattered Seas
Locations/The-Shattered-Seas.content:
The Starfall struck the oceans as hard as it struck the land. Across the Shattered Seas, patches of water boil permanently, trenches glow with starlight from below as if the sky fell into the seabed, and crystal reefs float just beneath or above the surface depending on the hour. Tides run in reverse in places, and standing waves hang motionless for days before collapsing without warning.
Few sailors cross the Shattered Seas by choice. Those who do tend to follow the routes anchored by Tiderest Shoals, the one stretch of calm within all this chaos, and the Crystal Reef that marks its edge.
Before the Starfall — The Inner Sea
Before Year 0, this body of water was called the Inner Sea by the western continent’s Coastal Leagues — the sea between the known worlds, navigable by those with the charts and the skill. It was difficult, seasonally treacherous, and long enough that miscalculation meant death. But it was understood. The League cities maintained island relay stations as crossing waypoints, and with Asterion’s star-charts, experienced captains completed the crossing in predictable time.
The Starfall fractured the seabed, destroyed the relay stations, submerged or displaced the waypoint islands, and introduced boiling zones, crystal growths, and tidal reversals that no prior chart was useful for. The crossing did not become impossible — Aaron’s people navigate it — but it became different enough that the League’s accumulated navigational knowledge was rendered useless overnight.
The name “Inner Sea” has not been used since Year 0. Nobody still alive remembers it well enough to use it, except possibly the Archivist, who has not chosen to.
Notable Figures

Aaron — chieftain of Tiderest Shoals, the calm anomaly within these seas.

Locations/The-Starfall-Crater.title: The Starfall Crater
Locations/The-Starfall-Crater.content:
A massive crater, visible from space.
Roughly continent-sized or slightly smaller.
Not perfectly circular — cracked, torn, collapsed inward.
Known to most simply as the World Scar, this is the site of the impact that ended the Age of Ascendancy. The Great Concord, capital of the Celestial Concord, stood here before the Starfall; its ruins are now scattered among the floating debris drifting above the basin, and purple and blue crystalline veins radiate outward from the impact site.
The land immediately surrounding the crater is known as the Dead Zones. Gravity behaves unpredictably here, sometimes locally inverting or pooling. Magic misfires or responds with a delay, as if the world itself is slow to react. Travelers report losing or gaining time in pockets near the rim.
Surrounding regions:

West — Ashenvale Pyrehold, home to Rhaegor’s Peak and Rhaegor
North — the High Sky Regions and Skybreak Zones
South — The Shattered Seas, the Crystal Reef, and Tiderest Shoals
East — Machine Wastes and Verdant Rupture
Scattered throughout — the Starfall Shard Zones

Notable Figures

Asterion — witnessed the Starfall directly and watched the Great Concord’s structures lift into the sky.
Serathiel — maintains a vigil at the edge of the World Scar, watching for what she believes may still be moving in the ruins below.

Locations/The-Subterranean-Kingdoms.title: The Subterranean Kingdoms
Locations/The-Subterranean-Kingdoms.content:
The Subterranean Kingdoms did not appear on any surface map, because they did not want to. They lived in tunnel networks beneath the eastern continent — primarily under the interior regions between the Molten Imperium and the Verdant Dominion — for a period that cannot be reliably dated because they kept their own calendar, used their own numerals, and never shared either with anyone above ground.
What is known about them comes almost entirely from Ka’Ruun, who is the last confirmed product of their forges. Ka’Ruun does not know when they collapsed, or why. He knows what they made, because he is what they made. He knows what they valued, because it is built into his geometry. He does not know what ended them. Nobody does.
Trade and Concealment
The Kingdoms traded with surface civilizations — consistently, over centuries — through a network of intermediaries who lived in surface communities and whose affiliation with the Kingdoms was known only to themselves. The goods that surfaced through this network were distinctive: crystals of unusual properties, manufactured components of no identifiable origin, occasionally complete mechanical artifacts with no visible means of assembly. The buyers did not ask where these things came from. The price of asking was that the supply stopped.
Both the Molten Imperium and the Verdant Dominion purchased from this network at various points. Neither knew they were buying from the same source. The Kingdoms found this arrangement satisfactory.
The Celestial Concord’s records show no awareness of the Kingdoms’ existence. Whether this is genuine ignorance or a deliberate omission — the Kingdoms requesting their absence from the record, the Concord agreeing — has not been established.
The Forges
The Kingdoms’ primary industry was the production of biomechanical constructs: living machines, organisms fused with crystalline and mechanical components, designed for specific purposes and then sealed with those purposes as permanent directives. Ka’Ruun is a siege creature — bred to shatter cities through flawless ballistic geometry. That this was a use case significant enough to warrant a dedicated construct type implies the Kingdoms had enemies, or anticipated them, or simply could not help building siege equipment once they knew how.
The crystalline components in Ka’Ruun’s construction — his spinal ridges, his firing mechanisms, the hollow cracks that pulse with light — come from a crystal vein system that exists only in the Kingdoms’ known tunnel network. The vein has not been found by surface explorers. Ka’Ruun has not gone looking, or says he hasn’t.
The Collapse
The Kingdoms went silent. That is all that can be said with certainty. There was no surface event that explains it — no war, no known catastrophe, no Starfall-equivalent. Ka’Ruun woke to silence and found the forges cold and the tunnels empty. He does not know how long he was dormant before waking. He says he was not dormant, that he has been continuously conscious since his creation, and that the tunnels were already empty when he first opened his eyes.
This is not consistent with the physical state of the tunnels, which show decades of undisturbed accumulation. Ka’Ruun does not comment on this inconsistency. He has been asked about it once, by Asterion, who noted the discrepancy in his field ledger and then did not press further.
The Starfall partially collapsed the tunnel network, sealing most of the deeper sections permanently. Whatever the Kingdoms left behind in those sections is not accessible by any currently known means.
One section of tunnel, in the northeast of the known network, shows signs of recent use. The accumulation there is disturbed. Nobody has confirmed who disturbed it.
What Ka’Ruun Carries
Ka’Ruun says “the crystal kingdoms will shine again.” He says this with the certainty of someone repeating a directive rather than expressing a hope. Whether this is a purpose built into him by the Kingdoms’ forges — a long-term mission encoded as instinct — or simply a phrase he learned and repeats because he has nothing else to anchor himself to, is not clear.
He is the only source of information about the Kingdoms that is still alive. He is not a reliable narrator. He knows this, and says so, and continues anyway.
Connections

Ka’Ruun — the last known construct of the Kingdoms’ forges; sole living source of information about them.
High Sky Regions — Ka’Ruun operates here; whether this is related to the Kingdoms’ purposes is unknown.
Machine Wastes — the surface above the Kingdoms’ primary tunnel network; the connection between the Wastes’ ruins and the tunnels beneath has not been mapped.
Molten Imperium — unknowing trading partner.
Verdant Dominion — unknowing trading partner.

Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.
(The entry above represents the complete extent of verified records on this subject. — Ed.)

Locations/Tiderest-Shoals.title: Tiderest Shoals
Locations/Tiderest-Shoals.content:
A floating village woven of coral bridges, kelp banners, and luminous tide-crystals, Tiderest Shoals is a pocket of calm inside the chaos of The Shattered Seas. Its waters are stabilized by the same tide-crystals that light the village, and ancient tide structures lie submerged beneath it — older than the village itself, and not fully understood by anyone living there.
The Shoals anchor the region’s water-aligned cultures and the dangerous but essential trade routes that cross the Shattered Seas. As chieftain, Aaron carries not only the ocean’s memory, but the weight of its future — and when the Starfall’s disturbance reaches the Shoals, it falls to him to meet it before it meets his people.
Notable Figures

Aaron — chieftain of Tiderest Shoals, a living stream given shape.
Thorall — an old friend of Aaron’s; the two share a bond forged by storms, tide and tundra united.

Locations/Trial-Chamber-Network.title: Trial Chamber Network
Locations/Trial-Chamber-Network.content:
Deep within Ashenvale Pyrehold, Rhaegor constructed an extensive network of trial chambers threading through the volcano’s magma veins. Each chamber was designed to test resolve, balance, and endurance, ensuring that only a worthy protector could reach what lay beneath the mountain.
Rhaegor believed that completing the trials would allow someone to find and wield The Eternis Core — a belief that shaped decades of his vigilance, and ultimately led him to Krysta. In truth, the Core chooses its own vessel. The trials were never a key, only a filter: a way of measuring worth, not a path to power.
Connections

Rhaegor — architect of the network.
The Eternis Core — the (mistaken) object of the trials.
Krysta — judged worthy of the trials by Rhaegor.
Ashenvale Pyrehold — location of the network.

Locations/Verdant-Rupture.title: Verdant Rupture
Locations/Verdant-Rupture.content:
The Verdant Rupture is a forest that, by any reasonable account, should not exist. It grew after the Starfall, fueled by an excess of life magic reacting violently against so much sudden death. The result is a landscape of bioluminescent flora and animals that have been warped by the same forces, yet remain gentle.
The Rupture is a study in contrast: soft, glowing beauty growing directly out of catastrophe, with a corruption that creeps at its edges, never quite breaching the canopy but never quite retreating either.
Notable Figures

Lumia — the Glittering Guardian, drawn to the Rupture’s light and its lost travelers alike.

Lore-and-Stories/The-History-of-the-Unna.filePath: Lore and Stories/The History of the Unnamed World.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-History-of-the-Unna.title: The History of the Unnamed World
Lore-and-Stories/The-History-of-the-Unna.content:
Long before the Starfall shattered the world, civilizations rose beneath a sky that was already breaking. Power does not descend from gods in this world — it leaks through fractures in reality itself. Erased constellations. Unstable magic. Cosmic absences that answer when observed too closely. The Starfall marked Year 0 and collapsed empires, rewrote geography, and scattered fragments of impossible power across the land, leaving survivors to rebuild amid monsters, relics, and half-forgotten truths.
What follows is the long account.

Era I — The Age of First Civilizations (~12,000 – 9,000 BCE)
Mortal civilizations emerge independently across multiple continents. Magic exists but is localized, ritualistic, and poorly understood. Early astronomy develops for navigation, agriculture, and religion. Asterion is born human during this era — exceptionally long-lived due to unknown astral magic, and obsessive about the night sky from the beginning. He does not inherit a great world. He helps build the idea of one.
Era II — The Age of Constellations (~9,000 – 6,000 BCE)
Asterion pioneers astral cartography — identifying the stable star-patterns that influence magic, fate, and natural forces, and developing Constellation Lines & Star Points as a discipline for working with them. Nations rise around star-aligned philosophies. Early star-resonant artifacts are created. Asterion’s immortality becomes suspected, then confirmed — not through myth but through his own celestial modeling, which shows him as a fixed point across millennia.
Era III — The Founding of the Celestial Concord (~6,000 – 4,000 BCE)
The Celestial Concord is founded as a transnational scholarly order dedicated to cataloging and safeguarding astral knowledge. Asterion is a founding authority — not its ruler, never its ruler. Massive white-and-gold structures rise: observatories, arcane academies, astral relay towers, all magically linked across continents. Celestial Concord HQ — the Meridian Library — becomes the seat of power. The Great Concord is built as the capital city. The world’s most advanced institution takes shape, and Asterion designs much of its infrastructure while avoiding its throne.
Era IV — The Gilded Age of the Concord (~4,000 – 2,500 BCE)
Concord influence peaks. They act as arbitrators between nations, keepers of magical law, developing star-powered enforcement divisions and institutionalizing astral magic. With that power comes subtle corruption: knowledge hoarding, political manipulation, moral absolutism. The Concord does not become evil — it becomes certain. Certainty is the more dangerous condition.
Era V — The Age of Omens (~2,500 – 800 BCE)
Astral anomalies increase. Some constellations flicker, distort, or vanish entirely. Asterion discovers that erased constellations are leaking back into the world and warns the Concord of a cosmic devourer entity responsible. Concord leadership dismisses his claims. Internal fractures form around the question of what to do about a warning no one wants to hear — fractures that eventually become Lumia’s preservation-focused sect and Serathiel’s judgment-focused sect.
Era VI — The Fracture of the Concord (~800 – 50 BCE)
Asterion is pressured out or leaves voluntarily — even he is uncertain which. The Concord, without its greatest architect and most inconvenient voice, becomes a militarized cabal: dogmatic, politically dominant, developing star-powered weapons and constructs, and treating faith in the Concord as near-religious. Meanwhile, Asterion continues his research in secrecy. The Concord rewrites records. Compresses his legacy. Protects itself from his shadow.
Year 0 — The Starfall
A god-like cosmic entity — possibly The Cosmic Devourer, possibly something else — triggers the Starfall. Massive meteoric impacts devastate the world. The Celestial Concord is obliterated; most of its leadership dies instantly, and its magically linked structures lose their connections forever. The World Scar is born. Technology and knowledge regress by centuries. The Eternis Core falls with the Starfall, embedding deep beneath the volcanic region of Ashenvale Pyrehold. New monsters and altered species emerge from the wreckage.
Asterion survives — not because he planned it, but because he was no longer centralized.
Era VII — The Shattered World (~1 – 10 AD)
The world becomes scattered survivors: villages, nomadic clans, isolated enclaves. Former empires are lost or mythologized. Rhaegor survives within his volcano and protects the surrounding region indirectly — including Cinderhearth, a village near Rhaegor’s Peak, where a girl named Krysta is roughly twelve to fourteen years old. She spends the years immediately after the Starfall defending the village from Starfall-born creatures, earning admiration and resentment in equal measure.
Era VIII — The Age of Shards (~10 – 30 AD)
Starfall Fragments begin surfacing worldwide. Their effects vary wildly: empowerment, corruption, environmental destabilization. New factions and proto-nations arise around them — the seeds of the Fragment Cults that now contest the Starfall Shard Zones. Rhaegor constructs the Trial Chamber Network within his volcano, believing the trials are the key to reaching the Eternis Core. They are not. The Core chooses its own vessel: Krysta, who becomes its chosen bearer after Rhaegor reveals himself to her, roughly ten to fifteen years after the Starfall. She now carries three voices: her own, the Core’s (order, preservation, control), and a third that has been present longer than either of them realized — Varesa’s corruption, which began posing as friendship years earlier. No one knows the full picture: not Rhaegor, not the village, not Krysta herself, initially.
See: The Fractured Heart, The Will of the Survivor, The Whisper in the Ash
Era IX — The Age of Awakenings (~30 – 60 AD)
Champions emerge worldwide. CR-9 reactivates in the Machine Wastes when Velrisa’s unraveling sends shockwaves through the world’s remaining arcane infrastructure. Garvak awakens. Ka’Ruun discovers volatile Starfall power in the High Sky Regions. Asterion resurfaces quietly, tracking constellation echoes that have begun manifesting in the people he encounters — fragments of erased star-patterns that should no longer exist, each one a clue in an unfolding celestial mystery. Rumors of a second Starfall spread.
See: The Dragon’s Temper, Starfire Trajectory, Neutralization Protocol, Siegeborn Awakening
The Current Era — The Unfolding Storm (~60 AD onward)
The world is fractured but awakening. Nations form with conflicting goals: control Starfall power, prevent another cataclysm, exploit what the first one left behind. Asterion hunts The Cosmic Devourer’s traces. The Eternis Core’s will strengthens within Krysta. Serathiel keeps her vigil at the edge of the World Scar, watching for something she cannot name. Lumia wanders the Verdant Rupture, tending to the lost. Thorall and Aaron maintain their alliance across the melting world.
The Starfall is not finished.
See: The Hollow Vigil, The Current That Chose to Move, The Mammoth’s Burden

For all recorded accounts, see The Starfall Anthology.
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.
This account supersedes the version dated ~45 AD. Differences between editions have not been disclosed.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: Beneath the Shifting Sky
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The night air was a sharp blade. Asterion stood in a courtyard where the sea spray hovered in mid-air, caught in a local gravity loop. He was teaching Maren, his apprentice, how to bleed color into the gaps of reality.
“It looks… fragile,” Maren said, her brush trembling.
“Fragile things endure longest,” Asterion said. “The Capital was made of stone and iron, and it is now dust. This lattice is made of attention.” He reached out, his fingers brushing a silver line of magic. It shivered, bending around his touch in a perfect curve. “Magic is no longer a tool, Maren. It is an honest conversation. If you forget that it is not yours to own, it will vanish.”
A tremor ran through the earth, the sea-loop collapsing in a roar of salt water. Maren stumbled, but Asterion remained a fixed point. “Do not fear the shift,” he said. “The sky is testing us. It wants to see if we’ve finally learned how to listen.”

See also: Asterion, Starfall Magic, The Shattered Seas
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Architecture of Preservation.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Architecture of Preservation
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
Garvak stood atop a pylon, his cloak snapping in the wind. Below him, his engineers winched a massive bulkhead out of the dunes. The Siegeborn knew that a wall was only as strong as its rarest component, and he needed this steel for his people’s salvation.
A subterranean hum vibrated through the sand. From the shadow emerged CR-9 — a massive, six-legged brass tank. It emitted a pulse of sound that made teeth ache.
IDENTIFIED: BIOLOGICAL UNAUTHORIZED EXCAVATION. STATUS: PRESERVATION BREACH.
Garvak hopped down, hammer ready. “My people need that steel to survive the winter. Stand aside.” CR-9’s turret clicked; it cared only for the integrity of the site.
As the titans clashed, Bogrund crouched nearby in his bulky power-suit, clutching his mace, Bonk.
“Look at the plating on that crab, Bonk,” Bogrund whispered. “If we peel off one fin while the Siegeborn has its attention, we power the forge for a decade.” A stray bolt pulverized the rock next to his head. “Or we die. Dying is also an option. Don’t look at me like that, you’re a mace.”
No further record of this encounter exists. The fin in question is unaccounted for.

See also: Garvak, CR-9, Bogrund, Bonk, Machine Wastes, The Ashen Seat
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The City of the Unmoving Reflection.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The City of the Unmoving Reflection
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
In the Capital, the wind was a curated melody. The city was a marvel of white stone, silver banners, and grand, orderly spires. The Celestial Concord had refined the Silent Veils until the weather itself was a matter of administrative decree. Asterion walked the Plaza of Constant Light, where the architecture was so precise that shadows seemed like a breach of protocol. He stopped by the Great Fountain, where the water fell in elegant, rhythmic sheets.
“The world is finally in its proper place, Asterion,” the High Prelate said. “No chaos. We have perfected the Reflection.”
Asterion reached out, his brush hovering near the water. It felt hard, resisting his touch with a dull, vibrating tension. “You haven’t perfected the world, Prelate,” Asterion said. “You’ve silenced it. This water wants to be a river, not a monument. You are building a debt of friction that this city cannot pay. Eventually, the reflection will shatter, and the dark will claim the pieces.”

See also: Asterion, The Celestial Concord, The Great Concord, The Starfall Crater
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Day the Earth Lost its Weight.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Day the Earth Lost its Weight
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony, Year 0.
(The phrase “the gravity has lost its resolve” appears verbatim in Asterion’s private field notes from the same date. I did not take it from his notes. I do not know why we used the same words.)
The Starfall began with the paint. Asterion was in the high vaults, finishing a map of the Western Reach. He watched as a droplet of crimson on his brush hovered, then drifted upward, joining a thousand other spheres of ink rising toward the ceiling.
“Gravity has lost its resolve,” he whispered.
Then, the impact hit. From the balcony, Asterion watched as the Great Spire shattered into massive, clean-edged blocks that drifted into the air, pulled upward by the meteor’s gravitational wake. Below, the ground opened like a jagged, glowing mouth. The World Scar was born in a flash of violet light, swallowing the center of the world.
“Master! We’re falling!” an acolyte screamed.
“No, boy,” Asterion said, standing tall against the roaring wind. “The earth is falling. We are merely being left behind.”
He watched his life’s work ascend into the clouds to become the High Sky, memorizing every fracture of the world he once knew.

See also: Asterion, The Starfall Crater, High Sky Regions, The Celestial Concord, The Cosmic Devourer
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Edge of the Circle.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Edge of the Circle
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The air in the council chamber was thick with the scent of old parchment and arrogance. Asterion sat at the periphery, his fingers tracing the rim of a chromatic sphere.
“The northern deviations are unacceptable,” a Governor stated. “If the tides do not align with our trade schedules, we must re-anchor the coastal stars. We have the right.”
Asterion rose slowly, his robes of shifting pigments catching the light. The room went silent. “I am neither malice nor mercy,” he said. “I am the Witness. And I tell you now: the sky does not recognize your schedules. You speak of ‘rights’ as if the stars are your cattle.”
“We are the Concord!” the Governor snapped.
“Then you shall define reality without me,” Asterion replied. “I will go where the sky remembers its own colors. When the friction finally breaks you, do not look to the stars for pity. They gave you a masterpiece, and you tried to edit the ink.”

See also: Asterion, The Celestial Concord
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The First Anomaly.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The First Anomaly
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The funeral was a silent affair of white silk and heavy incense. Asterion stood at the edge of the terrace, his fingers stained with the deep blues and violets of a mourning palette. He watched them lower Elara into the earth — his finest student, a woman who had mapped the tidal pulls of the inner moons with the stroke of a brush. Now she was dust, and he remained a static canvas, unchanged since he first taught her to see the soul in a sunrise eighty years prior.
“The Master is a painting that refuses to dry,” a deacon whispered.
Asterion did not turn. His eyes were fixed on the Southern Belt. A star there was shivering — a rhythmic pulse, like a heartbeat forced through a narrow throat. He felt a cold, sharp loneliness settle over him. He realized then that his immortality was a requirement of the Pattern; the universe was beginning to stutter, and it needed a witness who wouldn’t die before the sentence was finished.

See also: Asterion, Constellation Lines & Star Points, The Cosmic Devourer
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Friction of Being.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Friction of Being
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The tent smelled of ozone and damp fur. A young fragment-seeker was huddled over a shard of Starfall glass, trying to force it to emit warmth. The air around her was turning brittle, and frost began to spiderweb across her fingers — the world’s natural resistance pushing back.
“Stop,” Asterion said, stepping from the shadows, his brush trailing a line of warm amber light through the air. “You are shouting at a mountain and wondering why the echo is deafening.”
“I have to make it work!” she gasped.
“The world does not owe you its fire,” Asterion said. He relaxed his posture, letting his awareness of the shard soften. “The harder you define the heat, the more the cold must exist to balance it. This is the friction of being. You call it a curse. I call it the world’s way of saying ‘No’.” He moved his hand near the shard, and the frost vanished. “If you want to survive this age, learn to be a shadow. The sky does not answer those who try to rewrite its paints.”

See also: Asterion, Starfall Fragments, Starfall Magic
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Hollow Vigil.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Hollow Vigil
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The air at the lip of the World Scar felt unfinished. Serathiel stood at the precipice, wings of fractured light tucked tight. Her beam-bow was drawn, pointing into the violet mists. Her head moved in sharp, bird-like snaps, checking her arrows with obsessive, trembling fingers.
“The light must be absolute,” she whispered. “If the darkness moves, it is a confession.”
“You’re arguing with a hole in the dirt, Serathiel,” Asterion called out, limping up the slope with his brush and palette in hand.
“The hole swallowed the Law, Witness,” Serathiel said. “I saw a ripple in the fog near the Meridian foundations. It was unaligned with the vertical.”
Asterion looked into the Scar. He saw the ruins of the Capital — white stone now shattered and floating. “You cannot execute the wind, Serathiel. You are guarding a graveyard. The ‘Sin’ happened thirty years ago. You’re holding a grudge against a memory.”
Serathiel’s bow hand trembled. For a second, she looked like a veteran who had forgotten how to go home. Then, her eyes hardened. “The Law does not have a sunset. Something is coming up from the dark. I will be the last thing it sees.”
Asterion sat on a rock and opened his ledger.
Asterion’s ledger from this period has never been recovered.
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Treaty of the Melting World.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Treaty of the Melting World
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The meeting was held on The Great Shelf — a tongue of ice groaning under a rising sea. Thorall stood at the center, his tusks draped in iron chains. He was a straightforward man; he could smell the scent of a dying season. Across from him stood Aaron, the Tiderest chieftain, skin pulsing with blue light.
“The glaciers are bleeding, Aaron,” Thorall said. “The paths are turning to rivers.”
“And those rivers carry sickness to my reefs,” Aaron replied. “The water is losing its breath.”
Thorall looked at the source: a jagged Starfall shard embedded in the mountain peak, glowing violet. “I can crush that mountain, Fish-man. But the avalanche will bury your shoals. Or, I let it melt, and you swim over the ruins of my home. Neither is victory.”
Aaron stepped forward. “I can use the Ocean’s Curtain to draw the heat away, but I need your mammoths to haul the resonance-stones. We break the mountain together, or we drown in silence.”
Thorall looked at his lead mammoth. “Get your stones. But if a current trips a mammoth, I’m using your reefs as a bridge.”

See also: Thorall, Aaron, The Great Shelf, Tiderest Shoals, The Tundra Confederation
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Whisper in the Ash.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Whisper in the Ash
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The slopes were covered in a grey shroud of ash. Asterion watched Krysta training, her movements jagged and powerful. Rhaegor stood beside him, smelling of deep earth and cooling iron.
“She is strong, Cartographer,” Rhaegor grunted. “But her focus is brittle. The trials are weighing on her.”
“You are looking for a vessel, Rhaegor,” Asterion said, his eyes narrowing. “But for what? You treat that secret like a holy burden.”
“The sky needs an anchor,” Rhaegor said, his voice like grinding tectonic plates. “A power like that needs a bearer who cannot be moved. If she cannot find her center, she will never be worthy to touch what I guard. A weak vessel would only let the fire consume the world.”
Asterion watched Krysta strike, but she stumbled, her eyes darting toward the empty air beside her. For a moment, she looked terrified — not of the volcano, but of a shadow only she could see. Asterion felt the shiver in the Pattern, a subtle subversion he mistook for the girl’s own internal resistance.
(Asterion’s field notes from this period were later revised. The original reads differently.)

See also: Asterion, Krysta, Rhaegor, Ashenvale Pyrehold, The Eternis Core, Varesa
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Long Accounts - Asterion/The Will of the Survivor.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.title: The Will of the Survivor
Lore-and-Stories/The-Long-Accounts---Ast.content:
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony.
The black iron of the glaive was hot, but the sweat on Krysta’s brow was cold. She was ten again in her mind, standing in the mud of her village. She remembered the vibration in her grandfather’s rusted scythe as it met the bone of a scavenger. She hadn’t been “chosen” then; she had survived because she refused to be helpless.
He’s testing your obedience, Krysta, not your strength, a soft, melodic voice drifted through the sulfur.
Krysta didn’t look at Rhaegor on the ridge. She looked at Varesa, sitting on a jagged rock — a tall, elegant presence with eyes like a moonless night. To anyone else, the rocks were empty.
“He says if I don’t master the stance, the power will break me,” Krysta muttered.
“He wants to turn you into a pillar,” Varesa said, her touch icy against the heat. “But you survived the Starfall with a rusted scythe. You were already worthy before he ever looked at you. Why be a pillar for a world that already broke?”
Krysta raised her glaive, caught between Rhaegor’s demand for a Warden and Varesa’s promise of freedom.

See also: Asterion, Krysta, Varesa, Rhaegor, Ashenvale Pyrehold, Cinderhearth
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/A-Li.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/A Light for the Lost.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/A-Li.title: A Light for the Lost
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/A-Li.content:
Lumia knelt beside the dying traveler, hands trembling as she channeled a gentle glow into his wound.
The man coughed weakly. “You should… flee. The Starfall changed the forest. The beasts —”
“I know,” Lumia whispered. “That’s why I’m here.”
Fireflies gathered around her, drawn to her magic. They swirled in a gentle cluster, illuminating the darkness.
She focused harder, letting her light pulse with warmth.
Somewhere far off, the ground shook. A roar echoed through the trees.
Lumia looked up toward the tremor, eyes wide.
“That wasn’t an animal.”

See also: Lumia, Verdant Rupture, The Green Seat
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Asce.title: Ascension
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Asce.content:
In the midst of a siege, Serathiel stood atop a crumbled wall. CR-9’s bombardment thundered in the distance; Ka’Ruun’s starlance carved streaks across the sky.
Serathiel drew her string.
One condemned target below glowed with runes.
As her verdict struck, dawn erupted —
And Serathiel rose on incandescent wings.
The battlefield froze.
Judgment had come.

See also: Serathiel, CR-9, Ka’Ruun
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Bene.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Beneath the Molten Throne.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Bene.title: Beneath the Molten Throne
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Bene.content:
Deep within the volcanic labyrinth, Rhaegor felt the tremor before it hit.
The magma river rose, pulsing like a heartbeat. The cavern’s walls glowed bright red.
“Again?” Rhaegor snarled. “The Starfall stone dances restlessly.”
The lava beneath him churned. Beneath the molten lake, something old stirred.
He drove his flaming glaive into the magma bed. The lake stilled instantly.
“Who dares rattle my dominion?”
A pulse answered him. A rhythm. A cosmic resonance that did not belong to fire.
Rhaegor’s jaw tightened. An intruder.
He lifted his weapon and marched toward the surface, dragging molten stone behind him.
“Whatever crawled from that crater… I will return it to ash.”

Filed alongside — oral account, source unknown, collected ~30 AD. Provenance unverified. Included because the details are too specific to be invention.
The children sat cross-legged on the scorched earth outside Ashenvale Pyrehold, their wide eyes reflecting the glow of the ever-churning lava river nearby. The elder’s voice rose above the crackle of embers, soft but firm, carrying centuries of stories and warning.
“Long ago,” he began, “before your grandparents were born, before even the oldest stones cooled, the mountain was restless. Flames climbed higher than the sky, rivers of fire flowing unchecked. The villagers prayed, but no prayer could calm the volcano.
“Then came Rhaegor, the Lava Warden. Some say he was born from the mountain itself, others say he was a man who dared to wrest power from the magma. Wherever he walked, the earth bent to his will. Lava obeyed him.
“Sometimes he saves, sometimes he punishes. He serves the mountain. If you disturb its balance, it is his fury you will face. That is why we call him the Warden — because he watches, judges, and tempers the flames.
“And they say he knows things the mountain hides… secrets older than fire itself. There is a crystal deep inside the volcano, glowing with a light that can shape destinies. Some say Rhaegor has seen it, guarding it quietly in his own way. Some say he waits for the right moment… or the wrong one.”
*The children exchanged nervous glances, eyes wide with wonder and fear.

See also: Rhaegor, Rhaegor’s Peak, The Eternis Core, Cinderhearth
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Cond.title: Condemned
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Cond.content:
Garvak raised his war-cannon toward a village.
Serathiel’s voice cut through the smoke.
“You were warned.”
Golden seals closed around him like a cage.
Garvak laughed. “I have judged myself worthy.”
“Then dawn will disagree.”
A single beam pierced the battlefield.

See also: Serathiel, Garvak
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Embe.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Embers of Sanity.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Embe.title: Embers of Sanity
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Embe.content:
Velrisa’s candle flickered.
She’d lit it to calm herself, but the flame danced unnaturally, stretched thin as if trying to escape its wick.
A whisper echoed behind her.
You could burn so much brighter.
Velrisa froze. “No… not again.”
The whisper circled her mind like smoke in a glass jar.
You used to heal. You begged for peace. But look how they cast you aside…
Her hands trembled. She remembered the last time she held back. The last time mercy cost lives.
A second voice joined the first — her voice, speaking from somewhere deeper.
Ignite them. Heal yourself.
Velrisa grabbed the candle and crushed it in her fist. Hot wax burned her palm, and something inside her laughed.
Fire flickered from her fingertips.
The enchantress stood slowly, eyes glowing violet.
“I will soothe nothing,” she whispered. “Tonight, I set the world free.”
Behind her, the room lit with spectral embers — her sanity cracking like porcelain.
The candle was found still burning three days later. No wax had melted.

See also: Velrisa
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Neut.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Neutralization Protocol.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Neut.title: Neutralization Protocol
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Neut.content:
A sandstorm howled as CR-9 trudged through the desert.
The machine scanned the horizon.
THREAT LEVEL: MODERATE
THREAT TYPE: UNKNOWN METEORIC INCIDENT
PRIMARY PROTOCOL: INVESTIGATE. NEUTRALIZE.
Its internal core pulsed — Starfall energy warping its logic so subtly it almost seemed like emotion.
The machine detected distant tremors. Unknown entities. Unknown weapons signatures.
MISSION UPDATE:
TARGETS OF INTEREST DETECTED.
ENGAGING INVESTIGATIVE ORDNANCE.
It fired a shell.
Something screamed.
CR-9’s lens flickered.
THREAT RESPONSE: SUCCESSFUL.
MOVING TO NEXT TARGET.
The horizon does not scan back.
Probably.

See also: CR-9, Machine Wastes, Molten Imperium
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Sieg.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Siegeborn Awakening.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Sieg.title: Siegeborn Awakening
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Sieg.content:
The runes inside Garvak’s chest flickered. For the first time in centuries, he heard his gears grind.
Memory cores rebooted. Shields recalibrated. Weapons locked and loaded.
Across the cavern, a blue-white Starfall shard pulsed like a second sun.
Purpose identified.
Garvak rose to his full colossal height and marched toward the surface, carving a trench through stone.
The world above would soon witness the return of the Siegeborn.

See also: Garvak, Machine Wastes, Starfall Fragments
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Star.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Starfire Trajectory.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Star.title: Starfire Trajectory
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Star.content:
Ka’Ruun balanced on a floating basalt chunk, surveying the molten horizon.
“My trajectory was off,” he muttered, adjusting the dials on his gauntlet.
Teostra groaned. “Boy, you nearly vaporized the mountain’s spine.”
“That means it worked!”
The Starfall shard pulsed again, humming like a star’s heartbeat.
Ka’Ruun looked at it, eyes gleaming.
“You’re calling to something… and I’m gonna find out what.”
He fired a blast downward, launching himself into the sky, laughing like a mad comet.
Teostra watched him go.
“One day, you’ll explode,” he muttered.
Then, a tiny smile crossed his face.
“But until then… burn bright.”
He never came back down from that ridge.

See also: Ka’Ruun, Teostra, High Sky Regions, Starfall Fragments
Filed separately at subject’s insistence. See also: The Dragon’s Temper.
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The Current That Chose to Move.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The Current That Chose to Move
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
When the first whisper of Starfall reached Tiderest Shoals, the waters trembled. Waves rolled in unnatural patterns, and sea creatures fled deeper than the trenches dared allow. As chieftain, Aaron felt the disturbance like a bruise pressed against his spirit. Starfall had touched the land above… and soon it would gnaw its way into the sea.
So he rose.
From the heart of the Shoals, where tide-crystals shimmered around the sacred pool, Aaron emerged in full form — water sharpened by purpose. He gazed toward the horizon with a current’s steady resolve.
He remembered an old friend then: Thorall, the frost-tusked chieftain who once traveled beside him, tide and tundra united in a bond forged by storms. If Starfall threatened the land and sea alike, then the currents of fate were pulling them together once more.
“I will return,” Aaron vowed to his people. “But first, I must meet the storm before it meets us.”
With a sweeping surge, he left Tiderest Shoals behind — becoming a streak of shimmering blue racing across the world, determined to break the Starfall before it breaks everything he swore to protect.

See also: Aaron, Tiderest Shoals, Thorall, The Shattered Seas
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The Dragon's Temper.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The Dragon's Temper
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
Teostra sat atop a smoldering ridge, staring into the crater’s glow.
The Starfall shard pulsed with cosmic fire, its heat warping the air.
He snorted smoke. “An ember not of this world.”
A creature moved behind him.
Teostra didn’t turn. “It’s you, Ka’Ruun. You always step like a thunderbolt in a bottle.”
The boy skidded to a stop. “Teostra! You have to see what I found —”
The shard flared, and Ka’Ruun’s gauntlet blazed. Starfire danced wildly, out of control.
Teostra growled. “That rock will burn you from the inside.”
Ka’Ruun’s grin widened. “Then I’ll burn brighter.”
Teostra closed his eyes.
Foolish, brilliant child.

See also: Teostra, Ka’Ruun, High Sky Regions, Starfall Fragments
Filed separately at Ka’Ruun’s insistence. See also: Starfire Trajectory.
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The First Light.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The First Light
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
Serathiel walked through the ruins of the Concord’s Sanctuary, her steps silent on marble broken by centuries.
Where once a thousand adjudicators trained beneath dawnlight, only dust remained.
A flicker — twilight, not dawn — pooled behind her.
“Still mourning ruins?” Varesa’s voice, soft as silk.
“No.” Serathiel raised her bow. “Hunting what destroyed them.”
The arrow glowed. The shadow smiled.

See also: Serathiel, Varesa, Celestial Concord HQ, The Celestial Concord
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The Fractured Heart.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The Fractured Heart
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
The volcano groaned like a living god.
Deep beneath Ashenvale Pyrehold, the Eternis Core pulsed with fractured memory, its radiant facets casting broken light across the molten walls. For centuries it had kept the village alive — a guardian and a cage all at once.
From the Core’s wound, a shard broke free. She emerged humanoid, crystalline, facets glowing with raw magic. Her first breath resonated with the Core’s ancient voice:
Preserve. Control. Maintain order.
But another voice, softer and darker, slipped from the cracks of the mountain:
Break… unravel… let silence bloom.
The two voices collided in her mind. Her body trembled, shards grinding against themselves, and she screamed.
Above the tunnels, Varesa heard the sound and smiled. A ghost of twilight, she drifted like frost across fire, watching the corruption creep through the Core.
“Light fears me,” she whispered. “For even it casts a shadow.”
Elsewhere, lava dripping from his fists, Rhaegor felt the tremor. The mountain itself obeyed his fury.
“The ground’s waking angry.” He rose, molten stone trailing him, following the Core’s call.
Krysta stumbled through the volcanic tunnels, two voices clawing for dominance.
She entered a chamber where flame met shadow — and saw them: Varesa, a silhouette of darkness. Rhaegor, molten and towering.
Not allies. Not enemies. Just two forces drawn to the same fracture.
Varesa’s voice cut softly: “What a beautiful shard you are… breaking yourself to stay whole.”
Rhaegor’s voice rumbled like a quake: “She ain’t breaking. She’s choosing.”
Krysta’s chest burned with conflicting wills. Finally she whispered:
“I am here for a purpose… to protect the many.”
The Core flared in approval. The shadow recoiled in mockery. And the shard chose her path — between two entities, she would walk alone.
(The record here is incomplete. — )

See also: Krysta, Rhaegor, Varesa, The Eternis Core, Ashenvale Pyrehold
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The Mammoth's Burden.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The Mammoth's Burden
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
The wind howled like a wounded animal, whipping around Thorall’s furred shoulders.
He marched toward the Starfall breach, tusks heavy with frost. Behind him trudged his herd — warriors, shamans, and the last children of his dwindling people.
The sky shimmered with unnatural light. Purple cracks spread across the tundra.
“Velrisa’s curse,” Thorall muttered. “The land grows restless.”
A child beside him shivered. “Chief… will the Starfall hurt us?”
Thorall placed a massive hand on the boy’s head.
“No force can break us if we remain together.”
But as they neared the crater, the ground rumbled —
And something enormous awakened beneath the ice.

See also: Thorall, Frozen Fracture Tundras, Velrisa, The Starfall Crater
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/The Suit With an Attitude.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.title: The Suit With an Attitude
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/The-.content:
Bogrund’s workshop was always loud, but tonight it roared.
Steam hissed from pressure valves. Sparks showered the floor. A metal suit stomped in circles, swaying side to side like a frustrated toddler.
“Hold still, Bonk!” Bogrund shouted, tightening a bolt with both hands.
The suit ignored him, shaking like an angry kettle ready to blow.
Bogrund yanked his wrench free. “You want your ankle servos fixed or not?”
The suit slumped, groaning. Bogrund nodded. “Thought so.”
Outside the workshop, a red glow lit the night — the glow of the Starfall’s shards drifting from the crater far to the north. Everyone in the city felt the pull… everyone except Bogrund.
He had enough problems with the entity inside his suit.
Bonk tapped Bogrund’s shoulder, metal fingers clanking. It pointed to the distant crater.
“You want to go toward the giant sky-rock that’s making half the continent crazy?”
The suit nodded.
Bogrund sighed. “Bonk, buddy… if that thing wakes up again, we’re both in trouble.”
The suit thumped its chest with pride. Bogrund blinked. “Oh. You wanna punch whatever comes out of it.”
The suit nodded harder.
The engineer scratched his mustache. “…Alright. We’ll go look. But if we die, I’m haunting you.”
The suit saluted with perfect military precision.
They left the workshop arm in arm — man and machine — marching toward the sound of distant explosions.

See also: Bogrund, Bonk, Bogrund’s Workshop, Machine Wastes
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Xero.filePath: Lore and Stories/The Short Accounts/Xero & Rita.md
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Xero.title: Xero & Rita
Lore-and-Stories/The-Short-Accounts/Xero.content:
This page is a placeholder. Xero and Rita’s full story has not yet been written.
Xero is a survivor of the Starfall — not because he was strong, but because something chose him. Rita is the presence that answered when he refused to accept what was taken. No one else can see her. No one else can feel the weight pressing against their spine, until Xero lets her through.
She does not comfort him. She does not guide him. She promises one thing.
For the full account, see The Starfall Anthology — filed as [untitled], not yet received.
Connections

The Starfall Anthology — their story is listed but absent from the official record.
The Starfall Crater — Xero’s connection to the Starfall is personal and unresolved.

Lore-and-Stories/The-Starfall-Anthology.title: The Starfall Anthology
Lore-and-Stories/The-Starfall-Anthology.content:
These accounts have been gathered as received. Not all of what follows was given willingly.

The Overarching Record

The History of the Unnamed World — the long account. BCE through the present era.
When Paths Converge — the epilogue. Every path, one direction.


The Short Accounts
Filed by subject. Descriptions where available.

The Suit With an Attitude — Bogrund & Bonk — A workshop, a restless machine, and a direction neither of them chose.
Embers of Sanity — Velrisa — (no summary provided)
Beneath the Molten Throne — Rhaegor — The mountain speaks first. He answers second.
The Mammoth’s Burden — Thorall — A march toward a breach, and what the ground said before they arrived.
A Light for the Lost — Lumia — A traveler in the Verdant Rupture. Something in the trees that wasn’t an animal.
“The Arrow’s Shadow” — Varesa — (document unavailable)
The Dragon’s Temper — Teostra and Ka’Ruun — A ridge, a shard, and two different ideas about what “it worked” means.

The First Light — Celestial Concord HQ — Serathiel at the ruins. Varesa in the shadow. An arrow nocked.
Condemned — Serathiel, Garvak — A war-cannon raised. A verdict disagreeing.
Ascension — Serathiel — A siege, a judgment, and the moment dawn became something else.
“The Weight of Seven Stars” — (withdrawn)
[untitled] — Xero & Rita — (not yet received)


The Long Accounts — Asterion
Filed under Primary Accounts. Cross-reference: eyewitness testimony, 8,200 BCE — Year 0 — ~30 AD.

The First Anomaly — ~8,200 BCE. A funeral. A shivering star. The first suggestion that someone would need to outlive the sentence.
The City of the Unmoving Reflection — ~4,000 BCE. The Capital at its height. Asterion at the Great Fountain, touching water that had forgotten how to move.
The Edge of the Circle — ~1,500 BCE. The Council Chamber. The last time he addressed them directly.
The Day the Earth Lost its Weight — Year 0. The Meridian Library. Ink rising from a brush.
The Friction of Being — ~28 AD. A nomad camp. A fragment-seeker learning the difference between asking and demanding.
Beneath the Shifting Sky — ~25 AD. A ruined courtyard. An apprentice named Maren. The sea spray hovering in mid-air.
The Whisper in the Ash — ~30 AD. Ashenvale Pyrehold. Krysta training. Something Asterion misread.
The Will of the Survivor — ~30 AD. The Ashenvale slopes. What Varesa said while standing on rocks that appeared to be empty.
The Architecture of Preservation — ~22 AD. The Machine Wastes. Three parties, one site, no agreement.
The Treaty of the Melting World — ~25 AD. The Great Shelf. Thorall and Aaron, a mountain, and a question of whose catastrophe takes priority.
The Hollow Vigil — ~30 AD. The edge of the World Scar. Serathiel standing watch. Asterion sitting down and opening his ledger.


This catalogue supersedes the version dated ~45 AD. Differences between editions have not been disclosed.

Lore-and-Stories/When-Paths-Converge.title: When Paths Converge
Lore-and-Stories/When-Paths-Converge.content:
The crater grew brighter.
The tremors grew stronger.
And across the world…
A titan marched.
A machine rolled.
A boy flew.
A dragon snarled.
A sharpshooter nocked ghostly arrows.
A guardian glimmered in the dark.
A mammoth chief prepared his herd.
An enchantress burned.
A lava warden armed himself.
An engineer and his metal child marched to battle.
The Starfall called.
And everything powerful answered.

For the full account, see The History of the Unnamed World.
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.

The-Starfall-Universe.title: The Starfall Universe
The-Starfall-Universe.content:
Long before the Starfall shattered the world, civilizations rose beneath a sky that was already breaking. In this unnamed realm, power does not descend from gods but leaks through fractures in reality itself—erased constellations, unstable magic, and cosmic absences that answer when observed too closely. The Starfall, a cataclysmic celestial impact, marked Year 0 and collapsed empires, rewrote geography, and scattered fragments of impossible power across the land, leaving survivors to rebuild amid monsters, relics, and half-forgotten truths. From hidden volcano-wardens and corrupted cabals to immortal cartographers and children chosen by living crystals, the world’s champions are not heroes by destiny, but by proximity to a mystery older than memory—one that watches, reacts, and may one day fall again.
Map

Timeline at a Glance

Unknown BCE — Age of Ascendancy: Multiple advanced civilizations; arcane mastery, magitech, celestial observation.
~9,000–6,000 BCE — Age of Constellations: Asterion pioneers astral cartography.
~6,000–4,000 BCE — Founding of the Celestial Concord: see The Great Concord.
~4,000–2,500 BCE — Gilded Age of the Concord: peak influence, institutionalized astral magic.
~2,500–800 BCE — Age of Omens: astral anomalies, internal fractures (the philosophies behind Lumia and Serathiel emerge).
~800–50 BCE — Fracture of the Concord: Asterion departs; the Concord becomes a militarized cabal.
Year 0 — The Starfall: the cataclysm. The Great Concord is obliterated; The Starfall Crater is born; the Eternis Core falls and buries itself beneath Ashenvale.
0–10 AD — Shattered Age: survivors scatter; Rhaegor protects Ashenvale; Krysta is a child.
10–30 AD — Age of Shards: Starfall fragment discovered worldwide; Varesa begins corrupting Krysta; the Eternis Core chooses her as its vessel.
30–60 AD — Age of Awakenings: champions emerge worldwide (CR-9, Garvak, Ka’Ruun, and others); Asterion resurfaces.
~60 AD onward — The Unfolding Storm (current era): the world remains fractured; the Starfall is not finished.

Key Factions

The Celestial Concord — the lost order of astral scholars turned cabal. See The Great Concord and Celestial Concord HQ.
Fragment cults, city-states, and nomadic confederations that emerged after the Starfall. No global empires remain.

Key Systems

Starfall Magic — how magic is worked in this world, and what it costs.
Constellation Lines & Star Points — Asterion’s discipline for mapping the Pattern through the stars.
The Cosmic Devourer — the entity Asterion warned the old Concord about.

Notable Figures

Asterion — the Astral Cartographer, founder of the Concord, immortal witness to the Starfall.
Krysta — vessel of the Eternis Core.
Rhaegor — Lava Warden, guardian of Ashenvale.
Varesa — the Shadow Walker, corruptor of Krysta.
Serathiel — last loyal adjudicator of the Concord’s judgment-focused sect.
Lumia — inheritor of the Concord’s preservation-focused sect.

Note
Compiled by The Archivist of Starwatch Keep.
For a full relational map of all entries, see Concept Map.
